svg.title: Power BI Semantic Model Storage Modes: Import, DirectQuery, Direct Lake, Composite
svg.desc: An architecture diagram showing how Power BI semantic models connect to underlying data through Import, DirectQuery, Direct Lake, and Composite modes, detailing Direct Lake's OneLake and SQL flavors and the SQL view fallback trap.
svg.text: Power BI Semantic Model Storage Modes: Complete Architecture
VertiPaq Import · DirectQuery Live Pushdown · Direct Lake Zero-Copy · Composite Mixing · SQL Fallback Traps

g.title: Semantic model — An Analysis Services tabular model that reports, explorations, and DAX queries connect to.
g.text: The Unified Semantic Model (Analysis Services Tabular Engine)
Centralized business logic, DAX calculations, and relationship graph served to Power BI, Excel & API clients

g.title: Import — Data is copied into an in-memory VertiPaq cache and refreshed on a schedule.
g.text: • Full DAX & Power Query M power
❌ Long refresh times on big facts
❌ Risk of OOM on heavy refreshes

g.title: DirectQuery — Every query is forwarded live to the source; results always reflect current data.
g.text: • Translates DAX into SQL on the fly
• Zero model refresh time or size limits

g.title: Direct Lake — Reads Delta tables in OneLake directly, lazily, with no refresh step at all.
g.text: ❌ SQL flavor falls back on views / RLS
See Flavor Details in Bottom Panel

g.title: Composite model — Mixes Import, DirectQuery, or Direct Lake per table in one semantic model.
g.text: • Matches each table to optimal mode
• Fact Table: Direct Lake in OneLake
Best of both worlds in one model

g.title: Direct Lake on OneLake — Talks straight to OneLake APIs; never falls back to DirectQuery.
g.text: Flavor A: Direct Lake on OneLake
Points directly to ADLS / OneLake storage endpoints
• Uses Azure Data Lake Storage (ADLS) connector
✓ STRUCTURALLY CANNOT FALL BACK TO DIRECTQUERY
• Created by default in Power BI Desktop and Service
• Purest Direct Lake performance (0 SQL check overhead)
• If guardrails breached: query raises error instead of silent DQ
Microsoft recommended default for Fabric models.
Managed entirely via Workspace / OneLake RBAC roles.

g.title: Direct Lake on SQL — Mediated by the SQL analytics endpoint; can fall back to DirectQuery.
g.text: Flavor B: Direct Lake on SQL Endpoint
Mediated by SQL Analytics Endpoint for security & schema
• Evaluates SQL-endpoint RLS under delegated identity
• Created from SQL Analytics Endpoint modeling interface
• Fallback Triggers: SQL views, RLS, capacity guardrails
Required for delegated SQL RLS enforcement.
Applies T-SQL Row-Level & Column-Level security rules.

g.title: Trap: SQL views force fallback — A Direct Lake on SQL table built on a view silently falls back to DirectQuery on every query.
g.text: • Basing Direct Lake on SQL table on a VIEW forces
100% of queries against it into DirectQuery fallback!
Model still reports itself as Direct Lake in the UI!
• SQL views cannot be mapped to parquet files on OneLake
• Golden Rule: Always build Direct Lake models against
BASE DELTA TABLES, never SQL views!
Push view logic upstream into Silver/Gold Delta tables.
Inspect DAX Studio server timings or TMDL M expressions.

svg.text: Fabric Codex — Original Infographic, August 2026. Grounded in Microsoft Power BI & Direct Lake Internals Specs.
